mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 1.0% signals an easing monetary policy cycle that reduces discount rates applied to equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5% triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days as elevated unemployment signals weakening labor market conditions and reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rates (below 1.0%) and elevated GDP growth (GDPC1 above 16,000) creates a bullish feedback loop, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: convergence of monetary easing and robust demand
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite both proxies meeting their respective thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: During a rising unemployment trend (UNRATE increasing), elevated labor market stress reduces investor confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of rising UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing demand (HOUST exceeding 1200) indicates strengthening consumer confidence and housing market activity, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when HOUST exceeds 1200.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent high GDP growth (GDPC1 above 16,000) and elevated supply growth (INDPRO above 105) signal robust economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite both proxies exceeding their thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising), higher interest rates compress equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of FEDFUNDS increases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in employment (PAYEMS rising) reflects a strengthening labor market, fostering investor optimism and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite rising PAYEMS values.
